verses.text: “Comfort, comfort my people,” says your God.
“Speak comfortably to Jerusalem; and call out to her that her warfare is accomplished, that her iniquity is pardoned, that she has received of Yahweh’s hand double for all her sins.”
The voice of one who calls out, “Prepare the way of Yahweh in the wilderness! Make a level highway in the desert for our God.
Every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain and hill shall be made low. The uneven shall be made level, and the rough places a plain.
Yahweh’s glory shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together; for the mouth of Yahweh has spoken it.”
The voice of one saying, “Cry!” One said, “What shall I cry?” “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory is like the flower of the field.
The grass withers, the flower fades, because Yahweh’s breath blows on it. Surely the people are like grass.
The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God stands forever.”

You who tell good news to Zion, go up on a high mountain. You who tell good news to Jerusalem, lift up your voice with strength. Lift it up. Don’t be afraid. Say to the cities of Judah, “Behold, your God!”
Behold, the Lord Yahweh will come as a mighty one, and his arm will rule for him. Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.
He will feed his flock like a shepherd. He will gather the lambs in his arm, and carry them in his bosom. He will gently lead those who have their young.

Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and marked off the sky with his span, and calculated the dust of the earth in a measuring basket, and weighed the mountains in scales, and the hills in a balance?
Who has directed Yahweh’s Spirit, or has taught him as his counselor?
Who did he take counsel with, and who instructed him, and taught him in the path of justice, and taught him knowledge, and showed him the way of understanding?
Behold, the nations are like a drop in a bucket, and are regarded as a speck of dust on a balance. Behold, he lifts up the islands like a very little thing.
Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor its animals sufficient for a burnt offering.
All the nations are like nothing before him. They are regarded by him as less than nothing, and vanity.
To whom then will you liken God? Or what likeness will you compare to him?
A workman has cast an image, and the goldsmith overlays it with gold, and casts silver chains for it.
He who is too impoverished for such an offering chooses a tree that will not rot. He seeks a skillful workman to set up an engraved image for him that will not be moved.
Haven’t you known? Haven’t you heard, yet? Haven’t you been told from the beginning? Haven’t you understood from the foundations of the earth?
It is he who sits above the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers; who stretches out the heavens like a curtain, and spreads them out like a tent to dwell in;
who brings princes to nothing; who makes the judges of the earth like meaningless.
They are planted scarcely. They are sown scarcely. Their stock has scarcely taken root in the ground. He merely blows on them, and they wither, and the whirlwind takes them away as stubble.
“To whom then will you liken me? Who is my equal?” says the Holy One.

Lift up your eyes on high, and see who has created these, who brings out their army by number. He calls them all by name. by the greatness of his might, and because he is strong in power, Not one is lacking.
Why do you say, Jacob, and speak, Israel, “My way is hidden from Yahweh, and the justice due me is disregarded by my God?”
Haven’t you known? Haven’t you heard? The everlasting God, Yahweh, The Creator of the ends of the earth, doesn’t faint. He isn’t weary. His understanding is unsearchable.
He gives power to the weak. He increases the strength of him who has no might.
Even the youths faint and get weary, and the young men utterly fall;
But those who wait for Yahweh will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.

footnotes.content: "Comfort, comfort my people"—notice the word doubled, as if God can't say it just once. When sorrow sits heavy, this repeated summons reaches deepest: comfort is not whispered from a distance, but pressed close and spoken twice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jerusalem's warfare is accomplished, her iniquity pardoned—and she's received double from His hand, not as punishment but as full settlement. This is the mercy that leaves no debt unpaid, no shame unforgiven.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A voice calls in the wilderness to prepare the way. Every generation hears this call anew: not to build towers to heaven, but to make a highway for the Lord, clearing away what blocks His approach to us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every valley exalted, every mountain made low—the landscape of my heart, too, is remade when He comes. What I've hidden in the hollows, He lifts; what I've built as a wall, He lowers. All is leveled for His passage.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His glory shall be revealed and all flesh shall see it together—this is the promise: not a private revelation for a few, but a day when every eye turns toward the same light. This is what we're made for.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All flesh is like grass, all its glory like a field flower—it's not despair he's telling me, but honesty. We are small and temporary, yes. But that smallness becomes precious when held by hands that hold all eternity.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh's breath blows on it and it withers—there's something gentle, almost tender, in that image. His breath that sustains all life is also what passes over the things that cannot endure. We are held between those two truths.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God stands forever. This verse has anchored countless faithful through loss: the world's beauty fades, but His spoken promise remains—a rock beneath all change.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Behold, your God!" The herald's cry from the mountain—not whispered but proclaimed with strength, lifting the voice to shake the valleys. This is the announcement that needs no apology, no softening. It is sheer good news.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord comes as a mighty one, His arm ruling for Him, His reward with Him. The God of power does not arrive empty-handed—He brings recompense, the settling of all accounts, the making right of what was broken.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He will feed His flock like a shepherd, gather the lambs in His arm, carry them in His bosom, lead gently those with their young. This shepherd voice has comforted the broken and the fearful for centuries—the strength that gathers the fragile near.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Who has measured the waters in the hollow of His hand? The image undoes me—all that weight and vastness, reduced to something held in a palm. If I am smaller still, I am smaller held in infinite capacity.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Who has directed Yahweh's Spirit or taught Him as counselor? The question silences every voice claiming to advise the Almighty. All human counsel, by comparison, is a child's whisper in a cathedral.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Who instructed Him in justice and knowledge and the way of understanding? The answer is: no one. His wisdom stands alone. I can rest in knowing the One I trust needs no schooling, no correction, no improvement.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The nations are like a drop in a bucket, regarded as dust on a scale. He lifts the islands like a little thing. This is the perspective He invites me to—not to despise the world, but to see it truly: all in His hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lebanon is not sufficient to burn—Lebanon, with its vast cedars, could not provide enough fuel for an offering to match His worth. The geography and timber here anchor the point: even creation's grandeur falls short.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All nations are like nothing before Him, less than nothing, vanity. When the mighty of earth speak, it echoes from an inch above dust. Only in seeing His face does all ambition find its true scale.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "To whom then will you liken God? Or what likeness will you compare?" The question ends argument. We move from comparing sizes to recognizing that comparison itself becomes meaningless—He stands outside all categories.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A workman casts an image, the goldsmith overlays it with gold. Isaiah sees the futility clearly: we shape what we worship from what we've shaped. We fashion gods from the work of our hands—and then bow to our own making.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even the poor choose a tree that won't rot and seek a skillful workman to carve an image. The impulse to worship runs so deep that even poverty cannot stop us from crafting gods—all the more reason to know the true One.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Haven't you known? Haven't you heard?" The repeated questions almost sound like a grandfather's exasperation—gentle, but firm. How long have I been walking, and still need reminding? Yet He asks again, so I will know.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He sits above the circle of the earth, inhabitants like grasshoppers, stretches the heavens like a curtain. This verse gave shape to ancient understanding and still carries weight: the cosmos is His tent, and we are guests within it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He brings princes to nothing, makes the judges of the earth like meaningless. All authority trembles before His. Earthly power, which seems so final, becomes a whisper in the presence of the Eternal.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They are planted scarcely, sown scarcely, take scarcely root—and then He blows, they wither, the whirlwind takes them as stubble. The vulnerability is not cruelty but clarity: all power built on anything but Him is paper.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "To whom then will you liken me? Who is my equal?" says the Holy One. The repetition of the question drives it home: comparison has no answer because no peer exists. He stands utterly alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lift your eyes on high and see who created these, who brings out the stars by number, calling each by name. The stars know their Shepherd. I, too, am called by name—not lost among the multitude, but known and counted.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "My way is hidden from Yahweh, my justice disregarded by my God?" The complaint is real, almost anger—how long, Lord, before You see? Yet the question itself is answered by the verses that surround it: He sees all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The everlasting God, Yahweh, doesn't faint or grow weary, and His understanding is unsearchable. This verse has steadied countless who felt abandoned—His strength does not waver, His attention does not wane.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He gives power to the weak, increases the strength of those with no might. Not the already mighty, but the empty-handed, the spent, the broken—these receive His strength. This is where hope is born.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even the youths faint and grow weary, the young men utterly fall. No one escapes the exhaustion of living—not the strong, not the young. We all come to the end of ourselves. That is where He waits.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Those who wait for Yahweh will renew their strength, mount up with wings like eagles, run not weary, walk not faint. Readers today hear an echo in this verse—the waiting seems long, the exhaustion real, yet something always returns: the lifting wind beneath our wings, the breath that says: try again.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
